title: Silicon qubits surpass 99.99% gate fidelity while operating three at once
key_facts: Study in Nature Physics on a five-qubit silicon spin array
Dominant cause of fidelity loss in parallel operation: microwave-drive-induced a.c.-Stark shifts
Fix: pairwise phase calibrations with tailored pulses on a shared control line
Single-qubit X and Y gate fidelities well above 99.99%, some near 99.999%
Above 99.99% with up to three qubits running at once
Above 99.9% fault-tolerant threshold with all five running
Earlier silicon/silicon-germanium work saw 99.95% fall to 99.5% with two qubits
quote_evidence: Using tailored control pulses on a shared control line, we achieve primitive X and Y gate fidelities well above 99.99% for each qubit individually, with some approaching 99.999%.
Furthermore, these fidelities are preserved above 99.99% during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits.
During parallel five-qubit operation, fidelities remain above the widely targeted fault-tolerant threshold of 99.9%.
why_it_matters_hint: Parallel high-fidelity control through shared lines eases wiring for large silicon quantum processors.
notes: Phys.org blocked (403); read the Nature Physics paper itself (Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array). Author team and institutions not captured in the text read, so none are named.
